title: Jeremy Thomas
text:
Welcome to my website!
I’m a PhD researcher turned data scientist with 4+ years of experience analyzing high-frequency biometric and behavioral data.
My work focuses on quantitative modeling and prediction of human behavior, and translating messy experimental data into interpretable, decision-relevant models.
Across my academic work and applied projects, I’ve developed strengths in experimental design, causal inference, statistical modeling, and rapid model prototyping, primarily using Python.
I’m especially interested in problems where careful measurement and thinking matter as much as raw scale.
This site highlights projects that reflect how I approach data: formulating precise questions, validating assumptions, and building models that are both rigorous and practical.

title: Projects
text:
GitHub Repository
Python · Classification · Regression

Built an end-to-end modeling pipeline to predict product adoption across 25,000+ merchants using 1.5M+ transaction-level time-series observations.
Engineered temporal behavioural features from transactional time-series data (e.g., usage consistency and variability)..
Benchmarked regularized logistic regression against XGBoost using cross-validation, showing comparable predictive performance with improved interpretability.
Ranked the top 10–15% of merchants for targeted marketing and used model coefficients to identify key drivers of subscription adoption.

What I’d do next

Predict product adoption timing using survival based approaches rather than static classification

Validate targeting strategies via offline backtesting paired with online experimentation assumptions





Python · Experimentation · Unsupervised Learning

Designed and analyzed a large-scale motor learning experiment (10,000+ trials) using high-resolution motion-tracking data

Engineered kinematic time-series features and applied hidden Markov models to identify latent movement regimes.
Quantified individual differences in adaptation strategies, moving beyond group-level averages

Emphasized interpretability of unsupervised results

What I’d do next

Evaluate cluster stability using bootstrap or permutation-based methods

Extend the analysis to link inferred strategies with downstream performance or transfer effects
